name: Agent-computer interfaces (ACI). Canonical source: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering (Yang, Jimenez, Wettig, Lieret, Yao, Narasimhan, Press; arXiv:2405.15793, NeurIPS 2024), which coined the term ACI. Successors and adjacent work in this line: HyperAgent (arXiv:2409.16299), OpenHands/OpenDevin, Aider's repo-map, Anthropic's text_editor and bash tool definitions, MCP as a tool-surface standard, SWE-bench Live and SWE-bench-Verified as the moving evaluation substrate, and the tool-architecture ablation study The Devil Is in the Interface: Evaluating How Tool Architecture Shapes Coding Agent Behavior (arXiv:2608.11386). Related framings: 'From Human Interfaces to Agent Interfaces' (arXiv:2603.20300), 'Fork, Explore, Commit: OS Primitives for Agentic Exploration' (arXiv:2602.08199).
kind: Research result plus a design discipline, with an open-source reference implementation. Not a standard, not a browser feature, not a regulation. The transferable content is a set of empirically-supported interface design rules, not a component to install.
maturity: Production for the reference implementation (SWE-agent is actively maintained, MIT-licensed, widely forked) and research-active for the design question. The core claim -- that interface design changes agent performance without touching model weights -- is established and has been independently replicated in the 2026 tool-architecture ablation. The specific numeric findings age fast because they are entangled with model generation: SWE-agent's headline 12.5% pass@1 on SWE-bench was state of the art in mid-2024 and is far below current systems, so the NUMBERS are stale while the MECHANISM findings are not. Treat the design rules as durable and the scores as historical.
license: SWE-agent is MIT-licensed, so nothing prevents use, adaptation or vendoring here. The papers are arXiv preprints under standard arXiv licences and are citable. Nothing in this item is being adopted as code -- the value is the interface design discipline and the ablation numbers -- so licence is not a constraint.
keeps_and_discards: An ACI is a deliberately LOSSY view of an environment, and the whole finding is that the lossiness is what helps. SWE-agent's file viewer shows 100 lines at a time rather than a whole file, so it keeps a windowed slice plus navigation affordances (scroll, goto, search) and discards the rest of the file until asked. Its search tool keeps only the LIST OF FILES containing at least one match and discards the per-match context lines that grep would print -- the paper's own note is that succinct listing mattered. Its edit tool discards nothing but refuses: a linter runs on every edit and the edit does not go through if the result is not syntactically valid, so invalid states are kept out of the environment rather than reported after the fact. And empty output is replaced with an explicit message rather than silence. The generalisable rule is that an ACI keeps a bounded, navigable window plus an index, and discards bulk in favour of the ability to ask for more -- which is structurally identical to this project's 'pay for a node's child list, not the page'. The 2026 tool-architecture study extends the picture: a natural-language search interface increased access to relevant files by more than 11% and improved recall of high-relevance files at LOWER PRECISION, i.e. it keeps more and discards less, and that trade was net positive for exploration.
structure_preserved: The environment's own structure is preserved but re-presented: a repository stays a filesystem tree, and the interface adds line numbers, an explicit current-window indicator, and file-scoped search. Nothing is flattened. What is added is ADDRESSING -- the file viewer's line numbers make edits expressible as line ranges, which is the ACI equivalent of an address key and is what makes an edit command verifiable. The lesson for this project is that the interface's job is to make the environment's existing structure ADDRESSABLE and NAVIGABLE rather than to reorganise it, which is a structure-agnostic posture: SWE-agent never classifies a file as 'the important one' or a region as 'the relevant code'. Where later systems DO impose structure -- Aider's repo-map ranks files by graph centrality, HyperAgent assigns a Navigator role -- they are adding a relevance model, and the ablation evidence that removing the Navigator caused the largest performance drop in that system is evidence that the relevance model is doing real work, which is precisely the kind of help this project's constraints forbid.
interactive_elements: In the software-engineering setting the 'controls' are commands, and the ACI's contribution is that commands are FEWER, MORE SPECIFIC and GUARDED compared with a raw shell. The measured contrast is the sharpest number in this item: SWE-agent's ACI solved 10.7 percentage points more instances than the same agent given only a default Linux shell, on a 300-instance SWE-bench subset. A raw shell is strictly more capable and strictly worse. Translated to a web sensor, the analogue is that exposing every possible DOM operation to a model is worse than exposing a small, guarded set of navigation and expansion operations with predictable output shapes.
interactive_state_fidelity: The relevant fidelity here is STATE VISIBILITY rather than control state: after every action the agent must be able to tell what state the environment is now in, cheaply and unambiguously. SWE-agent's design answers this by making the file viewer's output self-describing (which file, which line window, how many lines total) and by making failure explicit -- the linter refusal tells the agent the edit did NOT happen, and the empty-output message tells the agent the command ran and produced nothing rather than leaving it to infer from silence. Both are cheap in tokens and both target the same failure: an agent that cannot distinguish 'nothing happened' from 'something happened invisibly' will hallucinate the state. This is directly applicable to a DOM sensor, where 'the click did nothing', 'the click succeeded and the page has not finished changing' and 'the click succeeded and nothing visible changed' are three different states that a naive interface renders identically.
layout_awareness: None in the original -- SWE-agent operates on text files and a shell, with no geometry anywhere. This matters for the project because it means the ACI literature's design rules were derived in a layout-free setting and transfer to a layout-free fold without modification. Web-agent successors that consume screenshots (covered in item 28) reintroduce geometry, and the ACI line is the one branch of agent-interface research that demonstrably does not need it: 12.5% on SWE-bench and 87.7% on HumanEvalFix were achieved with a purely textual interface. That is an existence proof that a well-designed text interface is sufficient for a hard, multi-step, stateful task.
javascript_required: Not applicable -- no browser is involved. The transferable point is architectural: the ACI is a thin layer of tooling over an environment, and it does not require the environment to be instrumented or modified. A web analogue that respects this would be a set of read and navigate commands over an already-loaded page, adding nothing to the page and requiring nothing of it, which is what the project's design already is.
evaluation_method: Task-completion evaluation with hidden tests, which is the strongest evaluation regime in this whole research set because the oracle is genuinely independent of the agent: SWE-bench takes real GitHub issues and their real merged fixes, and scores an agent's patch by running the repository's own tests, which the agent never sees. The ACI claims specifically are established by ABLATION -- hold the model fixed, vary one interface element, measure the change in resolve rate -- which is the right method for an interface claim and is rarely done. SWE-agent's ablation ran on 300 SWE-bench test instances. The 2026 tool-architecture study is methodologically stronger still: six interface architectures holding CAPABILITIES constant while varying only presentation, three different actor models (Qwen3Coder-30B, Kimi K2.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5), 65 instances from 25 repositories on the SWE-bench Live subset, 10 rollouts per instance for 11,700 trajectories total -- multiple rollouts being essential, since single-rollout agent evaluations are dominated by sampling noise. The weakness common to both is external validity: SWE-bench is Python, GitHub-hosted, test-covered repositories, which is a narrow slice of software and an even narrower analogue for web reading.
corpus_size_and_origins: SWE-bench full is 2,294 task instances drawn from 12 popular Python repositories; SWE-bench Verified is a 500-instance human-validated subset created after the original paper because a substantial fraction of the original tasks were found to be unsolvable or mis-specified -- a fact that retroactively qualifies every pre-Verified score including the 12.5%. SWE-agent's ACI ablation used 300 instances. The 2026 tool-architecture study used 65 instances from 25 repositories on SWE-bench Live, which is a deliberately fresher and more diverse origin set but a small one, compensated for by 10 rollouts each. So: origins number in the low tens of repositories, all Python, all open-source, all with automated test suites, all English. This is comparable in reach-narrowness to CleanEval's 58 English pages and should be quoted with the same care. Nothing in this corpus is a web page, so every transfer to a web-reading interface is an argument by analogy, not evidence.
reported_precision_recall: Reported as task resolve rates, with denominators. SWE-agent: 12.5% pass@1 on SWE-bench (denominator the full 2,294-instance test set, GPT-4-Turbo as the actor, mid-2024) and 87.7% pass@1 on HumanEvalFix. THE ACI ABLATION NUMBER, which is the one that matters here: SWE-agent's interface resolved 10.7 percentage points more instances than the same agent restricted to a default Linux shell, on 300 SWE-bench instances -- roughly a doubling relative to the base rate, achieved with no change to the model. The design-detail findings are reported qualitatively rather than as deltas: the 100-line file-viewer window was found to work best (window size was varied, but the per-size numbers are in the paper body rather than the abstract), the linter guardrail on edits improved outcomes, and succinct search output -- listing only files with at least one match -- was important. From the 2026 study, with denominators: a Python-code-block interface achieved similar task performance with 41.6% fewer steps and 56.3% lower token usage than a bash-only baseline, and reduced interaction steps by 33-41% across all three actors; an atomic structured-tool interface improved pass@k consistency for all three models with the largest gain for the weakest actor, up to 0.074 at pass@9 for Qwen3Coder-30B; a natural-language search interface increased access to relevant files by more than 11% with better recall of high-relevance files but lower precision; and lightweight text-based cognitive-scaffolding tools (hypothesis tracking, scratchpad) had limited effect, the authors' explanation being that actors project their existing reasoning patterns into such interfaces rather than changing behaviour. That last null result is as valuable as the positive ones and is the kind of finding vendor-run evaluations never publish.
independent_oracle: Yes, and it is the best in this research set: hidden unit tests written by the repository's own maintainers, executed after the agent finishes, with no shared assumptions with the agent or its interface. An agent cannot game it by producing plausible-looking output. This is worth dwelling on because it is exactly what web extraction lacks -- there is no equivalent of 'run the repo's tests' for 'did you read this page correctly', which is why the extraction literature falls back on human-annotated gold text and why oracle-free metrics (item 9) matter so much there. The ACI line demonstrates what becomes possible when a real oracle exists: you can ablate interface details and get trustworthy per-element effect sizes.
evidence_independence: Mixed and improving, and the distinction matters. SWE-agent's own numbers are author-run on a benchmark the same research group created (SWE-bench and SWE-agent share authors at Princeton), which is a genuine independence concern even though the hidden-test oracle limits how much it can bias results. The 2026 tool-architecture study is the important corroboration: different authors, three actor models including two the SWE-agent group did not use, a different benchmark variant, and it independently reproduces the central claim that interface architecture changes behaviour at constant capability. The specific interface RECIPES (100-line window, linter guardrail, file-list-only search) are author-reported and have not been independently re-ablated as far as this research found, so they should be recorded as the SWE-agent team's findings rather than as established constants. Leaderboard scores generally in this area are self-reported by submitters, and SWE-bench's history -- the need for a human-validated Verified subset -- shows that self-reported scores against an under-validated benchmark drift upward for reasons unrelated to capability.
page_archetype_coverage: Not applicable directly; the analogous axis is TASK archetype, and the ablation evidence shows the interface effect is not uniform across it. The 2026 study's clearest structural finding is that interface benefit is INVERSELY RELATED TO ACTOR STRENGTH -- structured atomic tools helped the weakest model most (up to 0.074 pass@9 for Qwen3Coder-30B) and helped strong models less. That is directly relevant to a project targeting small local models: interface discipline buys more for a 7B model than for a frontier one, so the design effort is well spent here and the numbers measured on frontier models understate what it is worth. The second differentiated finding is that exploration-heavy tasks benefit from broad, low-precision search while edit-heavy tasks benefit from guardrails -- different interface elements pay off at different phases, which argues for phase-appropriate rather than uniform interfaces.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Entirely unexamined. All benchmarks are English-language Python repositories with ASCII-dominant identifiers, so nothing in this literature speaks to CJK, RTL or non-Latin content. Two transferable hazards are visible from the mechanism nonetheless: any LINE-BASED window (the 100-line viewer) is a display unit that behaves differently when lines are long, and CJK text at the same line count carries far more content and far more tokens, so a fixed line budget is not a fixed token budget across scripts; and any CHARACTER-based truncation risks splitting multi-byte sequences or combining marks. A budget expressed in tokens or code points, not lines or bytes, is the script-invariant choice, and no paper in this line makes that choice explicitly. [uncertain] -- inference from mechanism, no measurement exists.
leaks_outward: In the SWE-agent setting, to the model provider: every observation the ACI produces is sent to the LM, so file contents, repository structure, error messages, environment variables surfaced by commands, and anything else the interface chooses to display all leave the local environment. This is the ACI's most under-discussed privacy property and it transfers directly and with force to a web sensor: WHAT THE INTERFACE DECIDES TO SHOW IS WHAT GETS DISCLOSED to whatever model is driving. A bounded window is therefore a privacy control as well as a token control -- showing 100 lines instead of a whole file discloses 100 lines instead of a whole file. For a page sensor reading authenticated content, the same logic means the projection's budget policy is also its disclosure policy, and that should be an explicit design statement rather than an emergent property.
mechanism_detectability: Not applicable in the original setting -- the repository does not observe the agent. The transferable observation is about the OTHER direction: the ACI runs commands in an environment, and any environment that can observe command patterns can profile the agent. For a web sensor, the actuator layer's actions (clicks, scrolls, navigations) are page-observable in a way that reads are not, so the ACI lesson to carry over is that the interface should keep the read path and the act path architecturally distinct, because they have completely different observability profiles. SWE-agent's own design already separates observation commands from mutation commands, and the linter guardrail applies only to the latter.
countermeasures: The ACI's own hardening is guardrails on ACTIONS rather than defences against an adversary: refuse an edit that would leave the file syntactically invalid; never let a command produce ambiguous silence; bound output volume so a single command cannot flood the context. Two of these generalise to adversarial settings and one does not. Bounded output IS an injection-relevant countermeasure -- a page cannot flood the model's context with attacker-controlled text if the interface caps what any single read returns, which turns a context-stuffing attack into a truncation the model can see. Refusal-on-invalid-state generalises to refusing actions whose preconditions cannot be verified. Neither addresses content-level adversarial input, which the ACI literature does not consider at all because its environment (a checked-out repository) is assumed trusted. That assumption does not hold for the web and is the largest gap when transferring these designs.
measured_fidelity_cost: Measured, unusually, and in the right units. The 2026 study is explicit that a Python-code-block interface achieved SIMILAR task performance with 41.6% fewer steps and 56.3% lower token usage than the bash-only control -- so the cost of the token saving was approximately nothing on the measured axis, which is a genuinely strong result and the only place in this research set where a compression claim is backed by a task-completion control. The countervailing measured cost: natural-language search bought more than 11% better access to relevant files at LOWER PRECISION, an explicit recall-for-precision trade. And the null result -- cognitive-scaffolding tools costing tokens and returning nothing measurable -- is a measured cost with no benefit. Against what control: bash-only, same models, same instances, ten rollouts each. This is the methodological template the extraction literature lacks.
gate_state_at_capture: No analogue in the software-engineering setting; the repository is simply present. The transferable point is negative and worth recording: the ACI literature assumes an environment that is fully and uniformly accessible, so it offers no design pattern for an environment that is partially gated, partially authenticated, or that changes its content depending on who is asking. Every one of those is normal on the web, and an interface design borrowed from this line will have no vocabulary for them unless one is added. Gate state should be part of the observation the interface returns, not metadata hidden from the model, precisely because the model's next action depends on it.
determinism: The interface is deterministic -- given the same environment state, the same command produces the same observation, and this is a design property worth naming because it is what makes ablation meaningful. The AGENT is not deterministic: sampling makes trajectories vary, which is why the 2026 study runs 10 rollouts per instance and reports pass@k rather than a single number. The methodological lesson transfers directly to this project: any measurement of an interface change against a model must be averaged over multiple rollouts, because single-run comparisons of agent behaviour are noise. A pass@1 difference of a few points between two interfaces on a single rollout is not evidence.
determinism_across_versions: Poor, and this is the field's biggest reproducibility problem. Every ACI result is a joint measurement of an interface and a model, and models are replaced continuously with no version pinning available for hosted ones -- so a result obtained with GPT-4-Turbo in 2024 cannot be reproduced, because that model's behaviour behind the same API name has changed and in some cases the endpoint is gone. The benchmark drifts too: SWE-bench was supplemented by SWE-bench Verified after validation problems were found, and SWE-bench Live exists to keep instances fresh, so scores across benchmark versions are not comparable. The practical rule for this project is that an interface decision justified by a published number should be RE-MEASURED against the model actually being used, because the published number's model is not available.
reproducibility: Better than most of this research set and still limited. Positives: SWE-agent is open source under MIT, SWE-bench instances are public with public tests, and trajectories are often published, so the harness is genuinely re-runnable. Negatives: the model is the irreproducible component, cost is a real barrier (11,700 trajectories is expensive), and benchmark versioning is messy. The reproducibility discipline this line demonstrates and that is worth copying is the publication of full trajectories -- the complete sequence of observations and actions -- which lets a reader audit WHY an interface helped rather than only that it did. A web sensor should log the equivalent: every observation the model was shown, in full, addressable.
failure_modes: From the papers and from the design rationale. (1) CONTEXT FLOODING: a raw shell command like cat on a large file dumps everything into context and destroys the trajectory; this is the failure the 100-line viewer exists to prevent, and it is the direct analogue of dumping a page's whole DOM into a model. (2) SILENT NO-OP: a command that produces no output leaves the agent unable to distinguish success from failure and it hallucinates a result; the explicit empty-output message is the fix. (3) INVALID INTERMEDIATE STATE: an edit that leaves a file unparseable poisons every subsequent observation, and the agent often does not notice; the linter guardrail refuses the edit instead. (4) LOW-SIGNAL SEARCH OUTPUT: grep-style per-match context on a large repository floods context with near-duplicate lines; listing files only was the reported fix. (5) TOO MANY TOOLS: the 2026 finding that cognitive-scaffolding tools had limited effect implies interface elements can cost tokens and attention while returning nothing -- an interface can be too rich. (6) CAPABILITY-BEHAVIOUR GAP: the study's headline conclusion is that equal capability with different architecture produces different behaviour, so 'the model could have done it' is not evidence that it will. (7) BENCHMARK MISSPECIFICATION, evidenced by SWE-bench needing a human-validated subset -- an interface tuned against a noisy benchmark is tuned partly to the noise.
failure_visibility: The ACI design tradition is unusually good on this axis and it is the single most transferable value. Its explicit rules are: never return ambiguous silence, refuse invalid operations at the interface rather than letting them succeed into a broken state, and make every observation self-describing about what state it reflects. That is an anti-silent-degradation stance implemented at the interface layer, and it aligns exactly with this project's stated refusal of silent degradation. The corresponding web-sensor rules write themselves: a read that was truncated must say it was truncated and by how much; a subtree that could not be reached (closed shadow root, cross-origin frame) must appear in the output as an explicit unreachable marker rather than as absence; an action whose effect could not be confirmed must report unconfirmed rather than success. Absence must never be indistinguishable from emptiness.
scale_limits: The binding limit is the model's context and attention, not compute, and every ACI design decision is downstream of that. The 100-line window, the file-list-only search output, and the suppression of verbose command output are all context-budget decisions. The 2026 study quantifies where the cost actually goes: interface style changed token usage by 56.3% and step count by 41.6% at constant task performance, meaning the interface, not the task, was the dominant cost term. Superlinearity appears in trajectory length -- each step carries the whole prior transcript, so token cost grows quadratically in steps unless the transcript is managed, which is why reducing step count by a third is worth more than the linear reading suggests. For this project the analogue is exact: an interface that makes a model take fewer, better-targeted expansions saves superlinearly, not linearly.
delta_cost_model: The ACI line has no explicit delta model -- environments are re-read on demand rather than diffed -- but it embodies a per-INTERACTION cost model that is the right frame here: each command has a bounded, predictable output size, and the agent pays per command rather than per environment. That is the same contract as 'pay for a node's child list, not the page'. What falls outside a bounded per-interaction cost, stated so the analogy is not oversold: (1) the transcript, which accumulates every prior observation and grows monotonically, so total cost is superlinear in interaction count regardless of how well each interaction is bounded -- the single most important exception and the one this project inherits directly; (2) unbounded-output tools, since any command that can return an arbitrary amount (a raw shell, an unbounded search) breaks the bound and reintroduces flooding; (3) environment state changes made by the agent itself, whose downstream cost is not attributable to the command that made them; (4) retries and error-recovery loops, which the guardrails reduce but do not eliminate; (5) the initial orientation cost of discovering the environment's shape, which is O(environment) and is what repo-map-style summaries try to amortise. Nothing here bounds cost against CHANGE, because the environment in these papers does not change underneath the agent -- which is the key disanalogy with a live page and the reason the project's O(delta) problem has no answer in this literature.
reanchoring_stability: Handled by using stable, human-meaningful addresses: file path plus line number, with the agent re-reading the window before editing rather than trusting a remembered offset. Line numbers are the ACI's positional address and they suffer exactly the ordered-tree fragility discussed elsewhere -- an insertion above shifts everything below -- which is why the workflow re-displays the window after every edit instead of accumulating offsets. That is a real and cheap pattern: RE-OBSERVE AFTER EVERY MUTATION rather than reasoning from a stale address. For a web sensor whose addresses are positional xpaths, the same discipline applies and is the pragmatic complement to the hash-based re-anchoring of item 23: do not carry an address across a mutation without revalidating it. No re-anchor rate is measured in this literature.
adversarial_exposure: The ACI literature assumes a TRUSTED ENVIRONMENT and this is its most serious gap for web transfer. A repository's contents are treated as data the agent reads and reasons over, with no consideration that a file could contain text engineered to redirect the agent -- despite the fact that SWE-agent reads issue text written by arbitrary GitHub users, which is precisely an untrusted-input channel. Nothing in the design distinguishes tool output from instruction, no observation carries a provenance marker, and there is no boundary marking in the transcript between the operator's task and the environment's content. Transferred to a web sensor unmodified, that design is maximally exposed to indirect prompt injection. The two ACI properties that incidentally HELP are worth keeping: bounded output caps how much attacker-controlled text can enter per read, and structured, self-describing observations make it easier to wrap environment content in an unambiguous, model-visible frame. The mechanism that must be ADDED is per-observation provenance -- every piece of environment content marked with where it came from -- which the trie key already supplies here and which the ACI literature does not have.
provenance_carrying: Partial by convention rather than by design. SWE-agent's observations are self-describing about their SOURCE within the environment -- the file viewer states which file and which line range -- which is genuine per-observation provenance and is exactly the pattern to copy. What is absent is a trust dimension: nothing distinguishes content written by the repository's maintainers from content pasted into an issue by an anonymous user, and nothing marks environment content as environment content rather than as instruction. For a web sensor the required tuple is richer (url, xpath, capture time, shadow depth, gate state) and the ACI's contribution is the format lesson: put the provenance IN the observation, adjacent to the content, in a form the model reads, rather than in out-of-band metadata the model never sees. Provenance the model cannot see cannot influence how the model treats the content.
roundtrip_safety: Not framed as round-tripping, but the linter guardrail is functionally a round-trip check: the edit is applied, the result is parsed, and if it does not parse the edit is rejected. That is serialise-parse-validate applied to a mutation, and it is the strongest form of the pattern in this research set because the check GATES the operation rather than merely reporting on it. The transferable rule: a projection that claims to be reversible should be validated by reversing it, and an operation whose result cannot be reparsed should be refused rather than recorded. Escaping is not discussed in this literature, which is a gap -- file content containing sequences that resemble the interface's own command or output syntax is a real confusion source and no paper here addresses it.
token_budget_and_ordering: This is the item's densest source of directly usable guidance and it is empirically grounded. The rules, with their evidence. (1) A FIXED WINDOW BEATS EVERYTHING-OR-NOTHING: the 100-line file viewer was found to work best, and the mechanism is that a bounded window with navigation lets the model choose what to pay for instead of paying for the whole file or getting nothing. The direct analogue is a text(budget=...) default that returns a complete, navigable frame rather than a truncated prefix. (2) TRUNCATION MUST BE VISIBLE AND NAVIGABLE: the viewer reports the window and total, so the model knows what it has not seen; silent truncation is the failure mode. (3) INDEX BEFORE CONTENT: search returns the list of files with matches, not the matches themselves, so the model pays for an index and then pays separately for what it chooses -- exactly the 'pay for the child list, not the page' contract, independently arrived at. (4) FEWER STEPS BEAT SHORTER STEPS: the 41.6%-fewer-steps, 56.3%-fewer-tokens result at equal performance came from letting the model express multi-operation intent in one code block rather than issuing many single tool calls, which matters because transcript cost is superlinear in step count. A sensor interface should therefore allow compound expansion requests, not force one node per turn. (5) INTERFACE HELP IS LARGEST FOR WEAK MODELS (up to 0.074 pass@9 for the 30B actor), which is the strongest available argument that this design work is worth more, not less, for a small local model. (6) SOME INTERFACE ELEMENTS ARE PURE COST: scaffolding tools that ask the model to externalise reasoning showed limited effect, so an element must earn its tokens by measurement, not by plausibility. On ORDERING specifically the ACI literature is silent -- it does not address where in the context high-value content should land -- so the position-bias findings from item 30 have to supply that, and the ACI rules constrain what is emitted rather than where.
representation_cost: Quantified for the interface-architecture axis: 56.3% token reduction and 33-41% step reduction from the Python-code-block interface at similar task performance, versus a bash-only control, across three models. That is the cleanest cost/benefit measurement available in this research set and its lesson is that presentation choices dominate content choices in total token spend. What is lost per token saved was measured as approximately nothing for that particular change -- which should be read as evidence that a large fraction of naive agent token spend is interface overhead rather than information, not as evidence that compression is generally free.
what_could_be_adopted: Six mechanisms, all directly applicable and none requiring code from this line. (1) THE BOUNDED NAVIGABLE WINDOW as the default read primitive, with the window size, position and total always stated in the observation -- the file viewer's 100 lines becomes a node-and-children frame with an explicit count of what was elided. (2) INDEX-THEN-CONTENT: return the child list (names, types, sizes, interactivity flags) as the cheap default and make content an explicit second request, which is the search-returns-file-list rule and is already the project's stated design; the ACI evidence is corroboration that it is the right one. (3) REFUSE-DON'T-DEGRADE, the linter guardrail generalised: an operation whose result cannot be validated is refused with a reason rather than performed and reported. (4) NO AMBIGUOUS SILENCE: distinguish 'read succeeded, subtree empty', 'read succeeded, output truncated at N', and 'read failed, subtree unreachable because closed shadow root' as three explicit observations, never as the same empty result. (5) COMPOUND ACTIONS to reduce step count, since transcript cost is superlinear in turns and the measured saving was 41.6% of steps at equal performance. (6) THE ABLATION METHODOLOGY ITSELF -- vary one interface element, hold model and task fixed, run many rollouts, report the delta -- which is how any claim about this project's projection should be justified, and which the extraction literature almost never does. Explicitly NOT to be adopted: relevance-ranked environment summaries (repo-map centrality, Navigator roles), which are exactly the pre-computed structural heuristics the project forbids; and the trusted-environment assumption, which must be replaced wholesale.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism: MIXED. The SWE-agent ACI core is ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- a windowed viewer, a file-list search and a guarded editor make no semantic judgement about what any region means, and the interface never names a file as important. The successor mechanisms that add a relevance model are REJECTED: Aider-style repo-map centrality ranking, HyperAgent's Navigator role, and any 'show the agent the important parts' summarisation are pre-computed structural heuristics by definition, and the ablation evidence that removing the Navigator caused the largest drop is evidence of how much such a heuristic contributes -- which makes it tempting and makes the refusal costly, and that cost should be acknowledged rather than hidden. NL-search-style broad retrieval sits at the boundary: it is ADOPTABLE ONLY IF the ranking is content similarity rather than structural role, since the constraint forbids naming regions, not ranking by query match. no_layout_in_the_fold: ADOPTABLE AS-IS -- the entire ACI line is layout-free and constitutes an existence proof that a purely textual interface suffices for hard multi-step tasks. o_delta: NEGATIVE ORACLE ONLY. The environment in these papers does not change underneath the agent, so the literature has no delta model and its per-interaction bound does not address incrementality at all. Worse, it carries a genuine exception this project inherits: transcript cost grows monotonically and superlinearly in step count regardless of per-step bounds, so a well-bounded interface still has an unbounded session. That must be named. no_mocks: ADOPTABLE AS-IS and exemplary -- hidden maintainer-written tests on real repositories are the strongest independent oracle in this research set, and the discipline of multiple rollouts plus published trajectories is the right model for how this project should measure its own interface. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: NO INTERACTION; nothing in this line touches browser internals. OVERALL VERDICT: the interface design rules are adoptable as-is and are the most immediately actionable material in this research set; the relevance-ranking successors are rejected on structure_agnosticism; the delta model is negative-oracle-only; and the trusted-environment assumption is a defect that must be repaired with per-observation provenance before any of it touches web content.
governance_signal_handling: None. The ACI literature has no notion of robots.txt, Content Signals, ai.txt, AIPREF, Web Bot Auth or HTTP 402, because its environment is a checked-out repository with no access-control layer. There is one adjacent and under-discussed issue: SWE-agent operates on open-source repositories whose licences govern derivative works, and neither the ACI papers nor the benchmarks discuss what licence obligations attach to model-generated patches derived from GPL-licensed context. That is the closest thing to a governance question in this line and it is unaddressed. Nothing transfers to web governance; those decisions belong at the fetch layer.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Two points, both structural. First, the disclosure point from leaks_outward: everything the interface shows goes to the model provider, so an interface's window policy is a data-transfer policy, and for a web sensor reading authenticated pages that means the projection's budget determines how much personal data leaves the machine per read. Making that explicit -- and preferring a local model precisely because it makes the transfer boundary internal -- is a design decision with a data-protection consequence, and this project's local-embedder posture already takes the right side of it. Second, the ACI literature retains nothing persistently by design: the environment is the source of truth and observations exist only in a transcript, so there is no stored-artifact question in the papers. This project does store, which means the regulated act happens here and not there, and no guidance is available from this line. Trajectory logging, which the reproducibility discipline recommends, is itself a persistent record of page content shown to a model and should be classified and retained accordingly rather than treated as ephemeral debug output. [uncertain] on any specific lawful-basis analysis under EDPB Guidelines 03/2026, which is item 19's subject.
